facts.text: Leverage rose because the NDS acquisition was funded from cash on hand and new borrowing while reported earnings barely moved. At 2026-09-30 the multiple was 1.60x on trailing EBITDA of USD 912,734 thousand: gross debt was little changed at USD 1,611,197 thousand against USD 1,611,823 thousand in March, but cash was USD 69,767 thousand lower. facts.text: Liquidity is adequate and maturities are back-ended. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is cash generation and the unused revolver. Trailing free cash flow of USD 529,952 thousand is 5.49 times trailing cash interest paid, the USD 750 million revolver is undrawn, and the issuer states that it complied with its covenants at 2026-09-30. The one maintenance test, a 4.25x senior secured net leverage ratio, applies only when revolver exposure exceeds 35% of commitments, so it does not apply while exposure sits far below that level. Reported EBITDA was also held back by restructuring and transaction costs of USD 48,299 thousand and USD 40,805 thousand in FY2026; on issuer-adjusted EBITDA net debt is 1.40x and Adjusted EBITDA grew 8.29% in FY2026. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against concern about policy is the size of the cushion it has not yet used. Free cash flow of USD 569,288 thousand in FY2026 covers cash interest comfortably, liquidity is USD 891.88 million with the revolver undrawn, buybacks in the first half of FY2027 were met from cash and operating cash flow, and the pro forma 2.30x counts no StormTrap earnings and only part-year NDS earnings, so run-rate leverage is probably lower than shown. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is cyclical, short-cycle and concentrated, with partly lagged pass-through pricing. Demand follows non-residential and residential construction, infrastructure funding and farm income, which the issuer links to credit availability and interest rates; the ten largest customers took about 50% of FY2026 net sales and the two largest distributors 25.8%, so volume risk sits with a few buyers who can switch suppliers on short notice. The annual report states directly what the Business & governance analysis recorded as not described, that many customers have no long-term arrangement. facts.text: Pricing power is real but lagged. facts.text: Free cash flow falls but stays positive because capital expenditures can be cut from about USD 200 million, working capital releases in a downturn, and the buyback, which with dividends exceeded first-half free cash flow by USD 43,939 thousand, can be stopped, while the dividend is small. The risk is sequencing: if StormTrap closes funded mainly from the revolver while payouts continue, revolver exposure could pass USD 262,500 thousand and bring the 4.25x covenant into force just as earnings fall, and at pro forma net leverage of 2.30x on reported EBITDA there is less room than at 1.60x. Management levers are enough to avoid liquidity distress in this scenario, because liquidity of USD 891.88 million and no bond maturity before 2030 give time, but they would have to be used. The primary downside path is a volume-led fall in margin colliding with leverage raised by acquisitions and buybacks. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Advanced Drainage Systems presents a strong business and financial profile supported by high margins, strong and flexible cash generation, ample liquidity and maturities that begin in 2030, but credit quality is constrained by customer concentration, volume and resin sensitivity, and a financial policy that has spent more than free cash flow on acquisitions and buybacks. Cash-flow durability appears adequate to strong, because underlying conversion is about half of Adjusted EBITDA and capital expenditure can flex. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on leverage at the time of the 2030 notes and 2031 revolver maturities, which is set by the next two years of payout and acquisition decisions. The primary downside path is a volume-led fall in margin meeting higher leverage while covenant terms are not supplied. Further analysis would require covenant and basket terms, StormTrap and NDS earnings and a stated leverage target. Fundamental credit analysis is complete. Top risk: releveraging through acquisitions and buybacks into a softer volume cycle. Basis: calculation F23; calculation F24; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

## Findings
### Bottom line

The supplied filings are sufficient for a credit snapshot of Advanced Drainage Systems, Inc. covering debt, liquidity and earnings, but not for covenant headroom, ratings or relative value, so creditor conclusions on those points stay open.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67

The five documents run from the fiscal 2025 annual report to the quarterly report for September 2026, signed on 2026-11-05, and carry the debt table, liquidity, the covenant summary and the pending USD 530 million StormTrap purchase. The credit agreement, the indentures, any rating, market quotes and the proxy statement are not supplied, and nothing dated after 2026-11-05 is available, so the closing of the StormTrap purchase is not established.

Financial foundation for Advanced Drainage Systems, Inc. (issuer wms-1604028), as of 2026-11-18, under the credit_snapshot pathway, covering normalised statements, debt and liquidity registers and leverage and cover metrics for FY2025, FY2026 and the twelve months to 2026-09-30 from the five supplied filings and the Source readiness analysis.
## Sources

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-11-05 | 738b2967c5c65047381d822e847c6976d9a7f7d8cb9904e0d100acf29a5d7200 | Latest balance sheet, H1 2027 and H1 2026 statements, debt, liquidity, EBITDA reconciliation, StormTrap agreement, held-for-sale entities, subsequent events. |

| Source readiness | CP-0 | 23f6923d4b99a0feff722a18f22f64453859a913d4b646fe6ecb557b3fd49aa2 | Source inventory, perimeter, conflicts already logged between filings, and the gaps on the credit agreement, indentures and StormTrap; its facts were re-read against the filings and none is corrected here. |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Advanced Drainage Systems is releveraging: net debt reached 1.60x trailing reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30 from 0.92x at FY2025, and the pending StormTrap purchase and continuing buybacks would lift it further, so creditors face rising leverage on a business that covers cash interest 9.46x.
Basis: calculation C06; calculation C04; calculation C37; calculation C25; calculation C38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28

Liquidity of USD 891.88 million and no scheduled principal above USD 32,675 thousand a year before fiscal 2031 on the March 2026 ladder limit near-term risk. What the supplied filings leave open is how StormTrap will be funded and whether the 4.25x springing covenant is then tested, because the credit agreement and the covenant calculation are not supplied.

Basis: calculation C48; calculation C50; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39
### Key findings

Leverage rose because the NDS acquisition was funded from cash on hand and new borrowing while reported earnings barely moved. Between FY2025 and FY2026 gross debt at balance-sheet value rose USD 350,300 thousand and cash fell USD 240,307 thousand, which lifted net debt from 0.92x to 1.59x of reported EBITDA, while EBITDA itself grew only 0.72%. At 2026-09-30 the multiple was 1.60x on trailing EBITDA of USD 912,734 thousand: gross debt was little changed at USD 1,611,197 thousand against USD 1,611,823 thousand in March, but cash was USD 69,767 thousand lower.

Basis: calculation C54; calculation C55; calculation C25; calculation C31; calculation C56; calculation C37; calculation C16; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C58; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 88; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5

Trailing EBITDA both flatters and understates the leverage picture. It holds NDS for only 240 days of the 365 days in the window, and the annual report's pro forma net sales for FY2026 with NDS owned all year were USD 239,316 thousand above reported net sales; the filings give no pro forma EBITDA, so run-rate EBITDA is probably higher than the trailing figure. The issuer's EBITDA also counts USD 35,968 thousand of interest income, other income and equity income, and on operating income plus depreciation and amortisation alone net debt is 1.66x rather than 1.60x.

Basis: calculation C77; calculation C97; calculation C74; calculation C75; calculation C37; calculation C73; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36

Interest cover is ample but easing. EBITDA covered cash interest paid 9.46x on a trailing basis against 10.05x in FY2026 and 9.71x in FY2025, because interest expense grew 18.23% and cash interest paid 22.16% in the first half of fiscal 2027 on the larger debt stack, while trailing EBITDA grew only 4.31% over FY2026.

Basis: calculation C38; calculation C32; calculation C26; calculation C64; calculation C65; calculation C57; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34

Cash generation is strong, but shareholder distributions now absorb all of it. Free cash flow was USD 359,489 thousand in the six months to 2026-09-30, down 9.86% as operating cash flow fell USD 51,596 thousand on working capital; buybacks and dividends took USD 403,428 thousand, USD 43,939 thousand more than free cash flow. A further USD 114.1 million was spent on repurchases after the quarter end, leaving about USD 563,195 thousand of the authorisation unused.

Basis: calculation C60; calculation C59; calculation C61; calculation C62; calculation C63; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43

Liquidity is adequate and maturities are back-ended. At 2026-09-30 liquidity was USD 891.88 million: cash of USD 153,245 thousand plus USD 738,635 thousand of undrawn revolver after USD 11,365 thousand of letters of credit, with the revolver maturing 2031-02-27. Only USD 7,955 thousand of debt is current. Scheduled principal at 2026-03-31 is no more than USD 32,675 thousand a year until fiscal 2031, when USD 506 million falls due, including the USD 500 million 2030 senior notes, followed by USD 1,071.5 million after that, which includes the 2034 senior notes and the balance of the term loan due 2033-02-28.

Basis: calculation C48; calculation C44; calculation C50; calculation C88; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 123

Claims outside the debt figure are modest against earnings but real. Finance leases of USD 161,909 thousand sit on their own balance-sheet lines, inside the issuer's own 1.6x measure but outside ours; operating lease liabilities were USD 74,199 thousand at 2026-03-31; redeemable KSOP shares of USD 69,045 thousand are mezzanine equity with a put right only if the stock stops being listed; and open equipment orders were about USD 80 million. The filings describe no defined-benefit pension, factoring or supplier finance programme and no fixed-price purchase commitment, and the guarantee of the South American joint venture's debt, capped at USD 5.5 million with nothing outstanding, expires 2026-12-31.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is cash generation and the unused revolver. Trailing free cash flow of USD 529,952 thousand is 5.49 times trailing cash interest paid, the USD 750 million revolver is undrawn, and the issuer states that it complied with its covenants at 2026-09-30. The one maintenance test, a 4.25x senior secured net leverage ratio, applies only when revolver exposure exceeds 35% of commitments, so it does not apply while exposure sits far below that level. Reported EBITDA was also held back by restructuring and transaction costs of USD 48,299 thousand and USD 40,805 thousand in FY2026; on issuer-adjusted EBITDA net debt is 1.40x and Adjusted EBITDA grew 8.29% in FY2026.

spans.text: ## Request

Business & governance for Advanced Drainage Systems, Inc. (issuer wms-1604028), as of 2026-11-18, under the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope: business model and revenue mix, ownership and control, governance, capital allocation, issuer history and the pending StormTrap acquisition, from the five supplied filings and the Source readiness analysis. Sponsor behaviour is assessed only where the filings document it, and no sponsor is named.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2025-03-31_wms_wms-20250331.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025 | 2025-05-15 | 7738155f6b90e060aa80bade5690ced698896e0d6f8802b9a0d6b5708fc05047 | Original business description, customer concentration for FY2025 and FY2023 and the first report of the Orenco acquisition, read against the later final amounts. |

| 10-Q_2025-12-31_wms_wms-20251231.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-05 | 530363203ab9ae869009bbb4db893878492f1a2cc0c101272c7e8ccebfcfab27 | Net sales of the nine months before the NDS closing; searched with the other filings for a stated leverage target. |

| 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-05-21 | d0a01784f7d26a22d30c6bced0450a0239cbb5e9fdf3e56fb600c8168c7dc5f5 | Business description, segment and product revenue, customers, ownership and anti-takeover risk factor, exhibit list, debt, acquisition, related party and equity notes, cash flow statement, controls and audit report. |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-11-05 | 738b2967c5c65047381d822e847c6976d9a7f7d8cb9904e0d100acf29a5d7200 | Latest revenue and segment tables, StormTrap agreement, held-for-sale entities, equity statement, repurchases, subsequent events, liquidity and controls. |
The document dates are the signature dates the documents print. The run settings are not issuer evidence and are not listed.
| Handoff | Module | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness | CP-0 | 23f6923d4b99a0feff722a18f22f64453859a913d4b646fe6ecb557b3fd49aa2 | Source inventory, perimeter and the gaps and conflicts already logged between the filings; its facts were re-read against the filings and none is corrected here. |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Advanced Drainage Systems has no named sponsor, so creditors depend on management's own financial policy, and that policy now spends more than the business generates, on acquisitions and shareholder returns, which makes covenant terms the filings do not show the real protection.

Basis: calculation A55; calculation A51; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 42

The operating base is strong, with segment margins of 28.89% in Stormwater and 43.59% in Wastewater, but growth is bought: net sales rose 5.03% in fiscal 2026 and 1.54% without the two acquisitions, and fell 4.50% in the September 2026 quarter without NDS. Two distributors take 25.8% of sales, and the pending USD 530 million StormTrap purchase and the USD 114.1 million of shares bought back since quarter end together equal 72.22% of the cash and revolver availability at 2026-09-30.

Basis: calculation A32; calculation A33; calculation A01; calculation A02; calculation A04; calculation A61; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28
### Key findings

Governance risk is medium, and it comes from financial policy rather than control. No named sponsor and a dispersed holder base remove the usual extraction risk, but a policy that spends more than free cash flow, a repeating acquisition pace and missing board and credit documents keep it from low.
Basis: calculation A55; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 75

No investor controls the company and no sponsor is named, so sponsor extraction and sponsor support are not in play and the discipline that matters is the board's own. Directors, officers and principal stockholders together hold about 16% of the shares and about 22% of the votes counting the employee retirement plan, and the filings name Canada Pension Plan Investment Board as party to 2021 shareholder and registration rights agreements without stating its holding or rights.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 2

Financial policy is elastic rather than conservative, and no stated leverage target bounds it. Over fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2026 acquisitions and shareholder returns together took 159.53% of free cash flow while the cash balance fell, and in the first half of fiscal 2027 buybacks and dividends alone took 112.22%, against 26.01% in fiscal 2026.

Basis: calculation A55; calculation A51; calculation A48; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 88; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 135; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39

Reported growth overstates demand: fiscal 2026 net sales rose 5.03% but 1.54% once NDS and the full-year effect of Orenco are removed, and the first half of fiscal 2027 rose 2.28% without NDS, made up of a rise of 9.22% in the June quarter and a fall of 4.50% in the September quarter, when volume in pipe and allied products fell while price and mix improved. The filings do not explain the swing, so the September decline cannot yet be called a trend.

Basis: calculation A01; calculation A02; calculation A05; calculation A03; calculation A04; 10-Q_2026-06-30_wms_wms-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–33

The business is moving from resin-linked pipe toward allied products and wastewater, which should dampen resin exposure if acquired margins hold. Domestic pipe fell from 50.87% of segment sales in fiscal 2025 to 43.50% in the first half of fiscal 2027, while allied products, which now include NDS, rose to 29.73%; Wastewater earned a segment margin of 43.59% against 28.89% in Stormwater in fiscal 2026 and supplied 30.70% of segment profit on 22.70% of segment sales, so a weak housing market would cut earnings by more than its sales share suggests.
Basis: calculation A08; calculation A18; calculation A19; calculation A33; calculation A32; calculation A36; calculation A16; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 49

Customer concentration is the structural business risk: two distributors took 25.8% of fiscal 2026 net sales and 27.0% in fiscal 2025, most sales run through distributors, and demand is seasonal, higher between April and September. A change in volumes or terms at one of them would reach earnings before any offset, and the filings give no contract terms.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 99

Acquired assets are intangible-heavy and partly for resale, so little of the price is backed by physical assets. Goodwill and identified intangibles are 78.51% of the USD 984.9 million paid for NDS, five NDS entities were held for sale on acquisition, two were sold in July 2026, and the first half carried a USD 29,818 thousand loss from classifying the rest as held for sale.
Basis: calculation A62; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 105–106; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16

The StormTrap purchase is the next test of that policy. At approximately USD 530 million it equals 59.43% of the cash and revolver availability at 2026-09-30, and 72.22% together with the USD 114.1 million of shares bought back after quarter end; the funding split between cash and the revolver, the agreement terms and any closing are not in the supplied filings.

Basis: calculation A60; calculation A61; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43

Reporting quality supports monitoring, with one open point: the annual report was signed 51 days after year end, the audit opinions were unqualified and internal control was effective, yet NDS, which carried 23% of total assets, was left out of the control assessment, so the largest recent addition has not been through a full control cycle.
Basis: calculation A68; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 74–75

Capacity to add debt grew in February 2026 and willingness to spend cash is shown by action, but the size of the capacity is not supplied. The amendment allows incremental facilities of up to the greater of USD 350 million or 100% of consolidated EBITDA and amended certain baskets, while the definitions that size them are missing, so capacity is described and not calculated; no priming, exchange or other creditor-adverse transaction is documented.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 119–120
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is cash generation and balance-sheet room. Free cash flow was USD 569,288 thousand in fiscal 2026, liquidity at 2026-09-30 was USD 891,880 thousand with the revolver undrawn, no bond matures before 2030, and shareholder payouts in the first half of fiscal 2027 were met from cash and operating cash flow with no revolver borrowings. A cut in buybacks, or a StormTrap closing funded mainly from cash flow with the revolver largely undrawn, would move the view toward low governance risk.
Basis: calculation A46; calculation A59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7

What would worsen the view is a debt-funded buyback or a revolver draw large enough to take exposure above 35% of commitments, which switches on the springing covenant; a further large acquisition before StormTrap is integrated; another quarter of falling volume excluding NDS; or credit documents showing wide payout and debt baskets. What would improve it is a stated leverage target, a proxy statement showing an independent board with credit-relevant oversight, and credit documents that cap payouts and additional debt.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67
### Limitations

- Sales growth excluding acquisitions is approximate because NDS and Orenco sales are printed in millions to one decimal and River Valley Pipe's sales are not separated; the claim that growth is bought changes only if the true figures differ by more than a few tenths of a percentage point.
Basis: calculation A02; calculation A04; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 54

- Statements that the company leads its markets, is the only national corrugated HDPE pipe producer and holds a cost advantage are management language that the filings do not test with market share data; they support the business-quality view only as management's own claim.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 21

- End-market mix is shown in charts that the extracted text does not carry, so exposure to housing, non-residential construction and agriculture is argued from segment and customer evidence; a printed split could raise or lower the cyclicality judgement.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 7

- Ownership percentages are as of 2026-05-14 and the share count has fallen 3.61% since, so insider and plan percentages may now be higher; the conclusion that no holder controls the company assumes they persist, and the stake of Canada Pension Plan Investment Board is not stated.
Basis: calculation A67; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1

- Because board and holder-level documents are absent, the governance risk level cannot be refined either way; it would move to low or high only on board independence facts, the size of the payout and debt baskets, or the terms of the 2021 agreements.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 77

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The pending transaction is the purchase of StormTrap Investments LLC under a definitive agreement entered on 2026-10-01 for approximately USD 530 million, funded by cash on hand and existing credit line capacity, with closing expected in the third quarter of fiscal 2027. The supplied filings do not show the agreement terms, StormTrap's earnings or any closing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43

The completed transaction that reshaped the company is NDS, bought on 2026-02-02 for USD 984.9 million, or USD 972.5 million net of cash, primarily from cash on hand. 78.51% of the price is goodwill and identified intangibles, NDS added USD 48.8 million of net sales in its first two months, and five of its entities were held for sale on acquisition.
Basis: calculation A62; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 105–106; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15

New debt was raised on 2026-02-27, 25 days after NDS closed: a USD 600 million term loan due 2033 and USD 500 million of senior notes due 2034, alongside a revolver raised from USD 600 million to USD 750 million and extended to 2031. The new debt refinanced the earlier term loan of USD 413.25 million and redeemed the USD 350 million of senior notes due 2027 at par. The supplied pages call the new notes senior but do not say whether they are secured or how they rank against the secured bank debt, and the revolver was undrawn at 2026-09-30.

Basis: calculation A77; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 119–120; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 122; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38

Shareholder transactions run alongside: a USD 1.0 billion repurchase authorization of February 2026 with USD 563.2 million left after the shares bought since 2026-09-30, and a quarterly dividend raised to USD 0.20 per share.
Basis: calculation A58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 47

Net debt was 1.60x trailing reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, and 2.30x pro forma for the StormTrap purchase (agreement dated 2026-10-01) and the share repurchase after the quarter end (no day stated), which are 2.18x and 1.72x taken alone. ### Key findings

The credit is strong today but weakening in direction, and the cause is financial policy more than trading. Total debt rose from 1.45x reported EBITDA at FY2025 to 1.77x over the twelve months to 2026-09-30 while earnings still covered cash interest 9.46x, and the StormTrap purchase and the repurchase after quarter end would lift net leverage from 1.60x to 2.30x pro forma.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1)

Business quality is strong but not defensive. The Adjusted EBITDA margin was 31.97% over the twelve months to 2026-09-30 and the Wastewater segment earned 43.59% against 28.89% in Stormwater in FY2026, yet sales follow construction and housing activity, and the ten largest customers took about 50% of FY2026 net sales, with many on no long-term arrangement.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 48; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Cash generation is a strength with room to flex. Free cash flow was 59.12% of Adjusted EBITDA in FY2026 against 41.45% in FY2025, it covered trailing cash interest 5.49 times, and capital expenditures of USD 249,766 thousand in FY2026 are guided to about USD 200 million in FY2027, 19.93% lower; cash taxes also fell 20.26% in FY2026.

Liquidity and maturities leave no near-term funding pressure. Liquidity was USD 891.88 million at 2026-09-30, only 2.87% of principal falls due before fiscal 2030, the first bond matures on 2030-07-15, and the USD 750 million revolver and the term loan run to 2031-02-27 and 2033-02-28; the February 2026 refinancing shows access to both the loan and the bond markets.
Basis: calculation F10; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 119–122; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The primary downside path is volume, and its first signs are already visible. Net sales excluding NDS fell 4.50% in the September 2026 quarter after rising 9.22% in the June quarter, domestic pipe sales fell 7.59% in the September quarter, and the Stormwater segment margin fell 1.48 percentage points to 29.49%, with higher material and transportation costs cited for Stormwater, so operating leverage and cost pass-through are already under test.

Financial policy is the swing factor. Cash returned to shareholders was 112.22% of free cash flow in the first half of FY2027 and acquisitions plus shareholder returns were 159.53% of free cash flow over FY2025 and FY2026, no leverage target is stated, and governance risk is medium because no named sponsor and a dispersed holder base remove extraction risk but not the board's own discretion.

The one maintenance covenant is a springing test that may become live. The 4.25x senior secured net leverage test applies only when revolver exposure exceeds USD 262,500 thousand, 35% of commitments, so a StormTrap purchase funded mainly from the revolver could switch it on; its definition and the issuer's ratio are not supplied, so headroom is not established.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against concern about policy is the size of the cushion it has not yet used. Free cash flow of USD 569,288 thousand in FY2026 covers cash interest comfortably, liquidity is USD 891.88 million with the revolver undrawn, buybacks in the first half of FY2027 were met from cash and operating cash flow, and the pro forma 2.30x counts no StormTrap earnings and only part-year NDS earnings, so run-rate leverage is probably lower than shown. A smaller buyback, or StormTrap earnings that prove large against its price of about USD 530 million, would move the view toward stable.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

What would worsen the view is a debt-funded buyback or a revolver draw above USD 262,500 thousand, a second quarter of falling sales excluding NDS, a further resin spike that the company cannot pass on, or credit documents with wide payout and debt baskets. What would improve it is a stated leverage target, StormTrap earnings and a closing funded largely from cash flow, a recovery of volume in the December 2026 quarter, and covenant definitions showing wide headroom.

### Company description

Advanced Drainage Systems makes thermoplastic corrugated pipe and related water management products for stormwater and onsite wastewater, sold mainly through distributors into non-residential, residential, infrastructure and agriculture construction. It reports two segments, Stormwater at 78.59% and Wastewater at 21.41% of FY2026 external net sales, and runs 64 manufacturing plants and 41 distribution centers that give it a national delivery footprint, which supports cost and service against regional competitors.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 15; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Cash-flow visibility is moderate rather than high. Orders are short-cycle with many customers on no long-term arrangement, sales are higher in the April to September half (55.08% of FY2026 net sales fell in the first half), and no backlog is published; against that, the customer base is large and the products are specified into long-lived drainage and septic installations, so debt service rests on strong margins and cash conversion rather than on contracted revenue.
Basis: calculation F08; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 20
### Ownership and group structure

The company is publicly held and no sponsor or parent is named: directors, officers and principal stockholders hold about 16% of the shares and about 22% of the votes counting the employee retirement plan, and charter provisions make a takeover harder. Creditors therefore face no sponsor-style recapitalisation risk and have no sponsor to turn to for support, and policy is set by a board whose independence and credit orientation are not established because the proxy statement is not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 42; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The borrower is the parent, and StormTech, Infiltrator Water Technologies and Orenco Systems guarantee the credit agreement; the joint ventures are small, with the issuer owning 51% of ADS Mexicana and 63% of EQ TruePointe One and guaranteeing at most USD 5.5 million of the South American joint venture's debt, which expires on 2026-12-31. The supplied pages disclose no holding company layer or unrestricted subsidiary designation, but the credit documents that would define them are not supplied and the ranking and security of the senior notes are not stated.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is cyclical, short-cycle and concentrated, with partly lagged pass-through pricing. Demand follows non-residential and residential construction, infrastructure funding and farm income, which the issuer links to credit availability and interest rates; the ten largest customers took about 50% of FY2026 net sales and the two largest distributors 25.8%, so volume risk sits with a few buyers who can switch suppliers on short notice. The annual report states directly what the Business & governance analysis recorded as not described, that many customers have no long-term arrangement.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 29; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Pricing power is real but lagged. In the September 2026 quarter price and mix improved while volume fell in both pipe and allied products, the issuer says allied products are less sensitive to resin prices, and it argues that conversion from concrete, steel and PVC to thermoplastic pipe continues as regulatory approvals widen; that conversion is management's view, and it protects volume only while thermoplastic stays price-competitive with the alternatives.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 49
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Resin is the main variable input: the company buys more than 1.0 billion pounds a year from about 450 suppliers, had no fixed-price purchase commitments outstanding at 2026-09-30 and relies on selling-price increases to recover cost, which the filing says can lag. Plants carry substantial fixed costs, so margin falls faster than sales when volume drops: against the prior-year quarter the September 2026 gross margin was 1.11 percentage points lower and the Stormwater segment margin 1.48 percentage points lower, even with NDS added.
Basis: calculation F18; calculation F15; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 32

Wastewater held its margin at 44.89% against 44.91% a year earlier, which locates the pressure in Stormwater, where the NDS mix and the resin-linked pipe and allied business both sit. Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure through recycled resin, diesel hedging and price increases, but a combined volume decline and resin spike would outrun those defences, since the filing warns that sharp resin rises can reach levels that cannot be fully passed through because of competing-product pricing.

### Capital intensity and free cash flow conversion

EBITDA converts to free cash flow well, but the year-to-year improvement is mostly working capital. Free cash flow was 59.12% of Adjusted EBITDA in FY2026 against 41.45% in FY2025, yet working capital added USD 81,171 thousand in FY2026 after absorbing USD 82,174 thousand in FY2025, and before those movements conversion was 50.69% in both years, so the underlying rate was stable at about half of Adjusted EBITDA.

Capital intensity is moderate and flexible: capital expenditures were 7.28% of trailing net sales and about USD 200 million is planned for FY2027, 19.93% below FY2026, including about USD 80 million already on order; cash interest takes 9.26% of trailing Adjusted EBITDA and cash taxes paid fell 20.26% in FY2026. In the first half of FY2027 operating cash flow fell 10.12% on working capital, but before working-capital movements it grew 12.93%, so the half's weakness is timing and the seasonality that puts 55.08% of annual sales in the first half. ### Porter's five forces

Competitive rivalry is moderate. The stormwater industry is highly fragmented with many regional specialists, the company competes with concrete, corrugated steel and PVC producers as well as other HDPE makers, and claims the only national corrugated HDPE footprint; rivalry is mostly on local coverage, availability and price, which limits margin only when volume is weak.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 20

The threat of new entrants is low to moderate. Entry needs a plant network that serves a shipping radius of about 250 miles, regulatory approvals from municipalities and state transport departments, and recycled-resin processing know-how, which protects returns on the issuer's installed base without preventing regional entry.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 24

The threat of substitutes is moderate and price-linked. Concrete, steel and PVC remain the alternatives; thermoplastic pipe has been gaining share on weight, cost and installation, but the filing accepts that a sharp resin rise can leave the company unable to pass costs through because of competing-product pricing, so substitution risk peaks exactly when resin is expensive.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 50

Buyer power is high. Two distributors took 25.8% of FY2026 net sales and the ten largest customers about 50%, many without long-term arrangements, and customer consolidation could move volume to competitors; the consequence for creditors is that a single customer decision can move sales and margin within a quarter.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 29; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Supplier power is moderate. Polypropylene resin suppliers are limited and high-density polyethylene suppliers are geographically concentrated, although the company buys from about 450 suppliers, holds multi-year supply agreements and processes its own recycled resin; supplier power therefore shows up as price volatility and a pass-through lag more than as a supply stoppage.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 14
### PEST analysis

Three categories are material to credit. Regulatory approvals and stormwater rules decide where products may be used and are a source of market access but also of delay; the economic cycle, interest rates and credit availability drive non-residential, residential and agricultural demand, and about 30% of new single-family homes use onsite wastewater systems, which ties the Wastewater segment to housing; and tariffs on resin or other inputs are a cost risk that the company may not pass on. Social and technological factors are not primary credit drivers on the supplied evidence.
### SWOT analysis

Strengths: a national plant and distribution network, procurement scale in resin, high margins and stable underlying cash conversion, regulatory approvals that widen the addressable market, and liquidity with back-ended maturities.

Weaknesses: customer concentration, a lagged resin pass-through, fixed-cost operating leverage, an intangible-heavy acquisition record that is still being integrated, and a payout policy that has outrun free cash flow.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 29; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Opportunities that could improve credit quality: continued material conversion, cross-selling allied products through NDS and StormTrap, onsite wastewater approvals, and a stated leverage target or slower buyback that would lock in the balance-sheet strength.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are a full year of NDS, price and mix gains, StormTrap adding engineered stormwater products, flexible capital expenditure and ample liquidity; the headwinds are the volume decline seen in the September 2026 quarter, resin and tariff costs, higher interest cost on the larger debt stack, the seasonally weaker second half, and execution on integrating two large acquisitions. No earnings guidance is published, and the only quantified outlook is capital expenditure of about USD 200 million in FY2027.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wms_wms-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1)

Over three to five years the debt structure is comfortable until the USD 500 million senior notes due 2030-07-15, which fall in fiscal 2031 with 34.27% of principal due by then, and the revolver due 2031-02-27; the structural tailwind is material conversion and wider approvals, and the structural headwind is that repeated acquisition and payout decisions, not business risk, will determine whether leverage stays moderate when those maturities are refinanced.

### Qualitative downside scenario

The most plausible issuer-specific downside begins with a housing and non-residential slowdown in the seasonally weaker second half, coinciding with a resin spike that the company cannot pass on quickly. Pipe and allied volume falls further after the 7.59% drop in domestic pipe sales in the September 2026 quarter, price and mix cannot offset it, and fixed plant costs push gross margin and the Stormwater segment margin down faster than sales, as the 1.11 and 1.48 percentage point falls of the September 2026 quarter already show.
Basis: calculation F18; calculation F15; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2026-03-31_wms_wms-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 32; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Free cash flow falls but stays positive because capital expenditures can be cut from about USD 200 million, working capital releases in a downturn, and the buyback, which with dividends exceeded first-half free cash flow by USD 43,939 thousand, can be stopped, while the dividend is small. The risk is sequencing: if StormTrap closes funded mainly from the revolver while payouts continue, revolver exposure could pass USD 262,500 thousand and bring the 4.25x covenant into force just as earnings fall, and at pro forma net leverage of 2.30x on reported EBITDA there is less room than at 1.60x. Management levers are enough to avoid liquidity distress in this scenario, because liquidity of USD 891.88 million and no bond maturity before 2030 give time, but they would have to be used. The primary downside path is a volume-led fall in margin colliding with leverage raised by acquisitions and buybacks.

### Overall credit view

Overall, Advanced Drainage Systems presents a strong business and financial profile supported by high margins, strong and flexible cash generation, ample liquidity and maturities that begin in 2030, but credit quality is constrained by customer concentration, volume and resin sensitivity, and a financial policy that has spent more than free cash flow on acquisitions and buybacks. Cash-flow durability appears adequate to strong, because underlying conversion is about half of Adjusted EBITDA and capital expenditure can flex. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on leverage at the time of the 2030 notes and 2031 revolver maturities, which is set by the next two years of payout and acquisition decisions. The primary downside path is a volume-led fall in margin meeting higher leverage while covenant terms are not supplied. Further analysis would require covenant and basket terms, StormTrap and NDS earnings and a stated leverage target. Fundamental credit analysis is complete. Top risk: releveraging through acquisitions and buybacks into a softer volume cycle.
